messages:
morgan: Heads up — after the kernel bump on prod-gpu-usw2 nodes a subset of GPU pods are Pending. Device plugin never finishes registration, kubelet shows errors.
liam: Ugh. Which nodes exactly? Exec logs? :eyes:
morgan: node/prod-gpu-12, prod-gpu-13, prod-gpu-14. Quick log snapshot from kubelet: 
```
Jun 04 09:12:03 kubelet[1234]: device-plugin registration failed: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = driver probe failed: modprobe nvidia: FATAL: Module nvidia not found in directory /lib/modules/6.1.0-101-generic
Jun 04 09:12:03 kubelet[1234]: error: nvidia-smi: initialization error: NVML: Unknown Error
```
devika: That looks like DKMS never compiled for 6.1 kernels. We had the kernel image rolled out yesterday (6.1.0-101). Our driver package was built against 5.15.
sofia: Which GPU operator/device-plugin versions are running? I remember a recent device-plugin change around unregister behavior.
rahul: gpu-operator v1.7.0, device-plugin v0.10.2 on those nodes. The operator DaemonSet for driver-installer ran but log shows compile failed for new kernel.
liam: Can you paste the driver-installer pod logs? Also check node /var/lib/dkms/* and dkms status.
morgan: driver-installer log snippet: 
```
Installing NVIDIA driver 525.116.04
DKMS: add completed.
DKMS: build error for kernel 6.1.0-101-generic (x86_64)
Error! Bad exit status from /var/lib/dkms/nvidia/525.116.04/build/make.log
```
sofia: So the installer didn't produce a kernel module for the new kernel — device plugin then can't bind and kubelet marks device-manager unhealthy. That's why pods Pending.
devika: Short-term mitigation: cordon affected nodes and drain GPU pods with --force -> then scale up a spare pool in another region/zone (or spin a small dedicated pool) so user jobs can continue. But that impacts cost.
rahul: We're already short on regional capacity, autoscaler couldn't get spare GPUs in us-west-2. If we drain too many nodes, we risk throttling inference capacity. Cost for on-demand replacement in us-west-2 is ~3x reserved.
liam: Can we roll back the kernel on those nodes to 5.15 quickly? What's the node image source? If they're using a custom boot image we may need infra help.
morgan: Nodes are using our standard instance image with config-managed kernel. Rolling back requires reprovisioning AMI or booting an older kernel via grub. That needs a reboot window.
devika: Alternative: rebuild driver for 6.1 in a canary and redeploy driver-installer DaemonSet with the built module instead of DKMS live build. That avoids node reboots and keeps node pinned.
sofia: Good idea — build validated driver modules in CI against 6.1, upload to internal artifact registry, then patch the driver-installer image to fetch prebuilt .run or .deb. Do a canary on 1 node first.
liam: Also check device-plugin flags: newer device-plugin exposes --skip-kernel-check which might let it register and surface partial GPUs? Not ideal. We should avoid surface of broken GPUs.
rahul: Ops-bot just alerted capacity alarms: "gpu_pool_usw2_utilization > 95%". We need fast plan.
morgan: Proposed immediate plan: 1) cordon prod-gpu-12/13/14 to stop scheduling new pods. 2) Drain non-critical GPU jobs and shift to reserved-dedicated-usw2 or us-west-1 burst pool. 3) Start CI build for driver+dkms for 6.1 (artifact tag drv-525-6.1). 4) Patch driver-installer DS to use prebuilt artifact and rollout to a single canary node. 5) If canary successful, roll to remaining nodes; else schedule kernel rollback and reboot window.
devika: I'll own CI build and artifact upload. ETA ~2h if no CI queue.
liam: I'll coordinate with infra for cordon/drain and try to provision 4 spot-backed GPUs in us-west-1 as temporary capacity. Expect cost increase.
sofia: Meanwhile I'll prepare a gpu-operator patch to add a preflight check: validate installed kernel module and fail early, plus a pod eviction hook so pods don't hang during driver restarts.
rahul: Agree on communications: posting to #incidents and paging a couple production SREs. Ops-bot: can you create an incident and page oncall?
ops-bot: INCIDENT created: INC-2026-1932 — "gpu driver/kern mismatch causing device-plugin registration failures". Oncall: @sre-oncall, pages sent.
morgan: One more note: we should update our upgrade playbook — include DKMS matrix for kernel versions we support and prebuild drivers for major kernel releases to avoid DKMS fragility. Also add node-feature-discovery label to mark kernel version so scheduler can respect until validated.
liam: Agreed. Also add a node taint for unvalidated-kernel=true:NoSchedule that driver-installer clears when module passes smoke tests. That will prevent scheduling during upgrade windows.
devika: CI build started. I'll update thread when artifact is ready.
sofia: Heads-up: if we have to reboot nodes mid-day, some critical inference routes may see degraded SLOs. Tell product so they can route low-priority traffic to backup region.
rahul: Adding a cost note: if the contingency requires renting extra on-demand GPUs for 24-48h, estimate $12k-$18k depending on scale. Approve? (cc @finance if needed)
morgan: For now proceed with canary prebuilt driver approach to minimize cost. I'll open a short runbook and paste here once done. :thumbsup:
